speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; have you noticed if the vomiting contains green fluid or blood, and has the baby passed any stool since birth?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Malrotation with midgut volvulus.

I have diagnosed this based on the classic presentation of bilious vomiting in a newborn, combined with the specific risk factor of a sibling who had pyloric stenosis, though the timing of symptoms (6 hours post-delivery) strongly points to a congenital midgut anomaly rather than hypertrophic pyloric stenosis. Given the life-threatening nature of this condition, immediate surgical consultation is required.
